title: Boox’s Beloved Palma E-Reader Gets Its Third Generation
gist: Boox announced three E Ink devices in September 2026 — the Note Air6 C and Note Mini C at $580 each and the smartphone-shaped Palma 3 at $340 — with only the Note Air6 C shipping immediately and the other two undated. All run Android 16, the two Note models share Kaleido 3 color displays and identical internals (octa-core, 6 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, microSD to 2 TB) differing only by 10.3-inch versus 8.52-inch screen size, and the Palma 3 moves to an aluminum build while being marketed as a low-stimulation second screen.

insights.claim: Boox markets the Palma 3 explicitly as a "low-stimulation second screen" rather than purely as an e-reader, positioning E Ink hardware as an antidote to smartphone attention capture.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: The digital-wellbeing framing is becoming a hardware product category, not just an app feature — a durable niche demand driver for E Ink panel makers.
insights.quote: Boox promotes this as a low-stimulation second screen
insights.locator: Size also comes into play for Boox’s final

insights.claim: The Palma line's defining bet is form factor rather than display capability — a palm-sized, smartphone-shaped device with a 6.13-inch non-color E Ink screen, dual-tone front light and ambient light sensor.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Pocketability, not color or speed, is what made this line popular; competitors targeting the segment should optimize size before panel specs.
insights.locator: It’s another E Ink screen device with an Android 16 base

insights.claim: The Palma 3 upgrades from the Palma 2's plastic design to an aluminum build while retaining the rear camera (promoted on the prior generation for document scanning rather than photography), dual microphones and a customizable smart button.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Materials upgrades with carried-over internals is the classic mature-product playbook — incremental premiumization to hold price against cheaper entrants.
insights.locator: The Palma 3 also has an aluminum build

insights.claim: Boox launched the Note Air6 C at $580, the Note Mini C at the same $580, and the Palma 3 at $340, creating a ladder where the smaller Note commands no discount versus the larger one.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Identical pricing across sizes signals cost is dominated by the color panel and SoC, not screen area — margin structure differs sharply from LCD/OLED tablets.
insights.locator: Boox launched three new E Ink products

insights.claim: The Note Mini C and Note Air6 C share an octa-core processor, 6 GB of RAM, 64 GB of storage and microSD expansion to 2 TB, differing only in 8.52-inch versus 10.3-inch Kaleido 3 color displays.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Spec-identical SKUs differentiated only by size indicate a single hardware platform amortized across models — a cost efficiency but also a commoditization risk.
insights.quote: Overall, it's more about size than it is power if you're choosing between them
insights.locator: The Mini C and Air6 have fairly similar specs

insights.claim: Only the Note Air6 C is available at announcement; both the Note Mini C and the Palma 3 have no release date beyond "coming soon" and "soon," a paper-launch pattern for the two more novel SKUs.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Undated availability on the most anticipated model suggests supply or panel-sourcing constraints; treat announced-but-unshipped E Ink SKUs skeptically.
insights.locator: Out of the three devices announced

themes.theme: E Ink devices as Android tablets

insights.claim: All three new Boox devices run Android 16, with the Note Air6 C explicitly described as delivering a more tablet-style user interface and app access — making these general-purpose Android tablets with E Ink panels rather than dedicated readers.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Full Android on E Ink erodes the walled-garden advantage of Kindle-style readers and opens the category to the entire app ecosystem.

insights.claim: Boox is layering AI features onto E Ink notebooks — including meeting and audio insights plus document summarization — alongside a Dual Notes firmware feature for annotating two documents side by side.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: AI summarization is reaching even low-power niche hardware, suggesting assistant features are now a checkbox requirement across all device categories.
insights.locator: The Note Air6 C also has new firmware

insights.claim: The reviewer frames the Palma 3's key competitive comparison against smaller rivals such as the Xteink, indicating the palm-sized E Ink niche now has direct competitors rather than being a Boox monopoly.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Emerging competition in pocket E Ink suggests the category has validated demand; watch for price compression at the $300-350 tier.
insights.quote: I'm most interested in how it will compare against smaller models like the Xteink.

insights.claim: Boox timed its multi-product launch to the fall tech-release window immediately following Apple's annual September iPhone event, competing for attention in the same news cycle as far larger launches.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Niche hardware clustering around Apple's event window is a low-cost attention arbitrage; useful context for reading fall launch density.
